Hi all — I reviewed the draft and attached a focused set of redlines (redlines_marissa_comments.pdf) that address the three priority items: term, SLA credits, and billing/proration. Highlights:

- Term: proposed 24-month effective term with explicit renewal notice windows and a carve-out for early termination tied to insolvency/force majeure.
- SLA credits: suggested language that keeps credits as an offsets mechanism (credit against future invoices) with a quarterly cap equal to one month's average fees for the impacted service tier. Also added escalation path and measurement method (99th percentile measured across a rolling 30-day window).
- Billing/proration: suggested ops-friendly approach — invoice-based proration at milestone transitions with a one-time invoice adjustment on the month following a milestone being met. This avoids retrospective credit blips on customer invoices.

Open questions for Acme: is the quarterly cap acceptable? If not, what alternative cap do you prefer (percentage of quarterly fees, fixed dollars, or tiered caps by severity)? Also please confirm the exact milestone trigger definitions (API traffic threshold vs. signed acceptance).

I'll hold the rest of the MSA changes until we lock SLA/billing mechanics. Jordan — let me know if you want me to include indemnity and data retention clarifications in this pass.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
